content.value_statement: AI-assisted coding can miss tests, security checks, and release criteria. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a staged checklist for safer delivery.
actual_capabilities: Defines pre-implementation, implementation, testing, and review gates for coding agents.
Lists concrete validation commands for TypeScript, tests, linting, builds, and secret checks.
Documents security checks for input validation, authorization, SQL injection, and hardcoded secrets.
Provides examples of acceptable and blocked TypeScript, API, database, and test patterns.
Includes a Python aggregator that runs related validator scripts when installed in a project.
limitations: The included validator depends on other skill validator scripts being present in the project.
Most checks are guidance or shell commands, not a complete automated policy engine.
Manual review is still required for architecture, authorization, and business logic risks.
The examples focus on TypeScript, React, Next.js, Prisma, and Vitest-style projects.

use_cases.title: Prepare implementation
use_cases.description: Review requirements, architecture, types, dependencies, and security concerns before code changes begin.

use_cases.title: Validate a pull request
use_cases.description: Run staged checks for TypeScript, tests, coverage, security, documentation, and build readiness.

use_cases.title: Standardize team delivery
use_cases.description: Use one checklist to align agents and reviewers on repeatable quality expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Run the basic gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality-gates skill to check my current change. Start with the pre-implementation gate and list missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Check implementation quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-gates to review the implementation gate for this branch. Check TypeScript strictness, validation, error handling, and secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit tests and coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-gates to inspect the testing gate. Identify missing AAA structure, weak UI assertions, skipped tests, and coverage gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Perform release readiness review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-gates to run the final review gate. Combine code review, security, build, tests, and documentation checks into one action list.

output_examples.input: Check whether this feature is ready for review.
output: Pre-implementation gate passed because requirements and architecture are documented.
Implementation gate needs input validation on the new API route.
Testing gate needs one integration test for the error path.

output_examples.input: Review my tests for quality gate compliance.
output_examples.output: The tests cover the happy path and one failure path. Add DOM state assertions for the UI change and remove the focused test before merging.

output_examples.input: Prepare a final quality gate summary.
output: TypeScript, lint, tests, and build should run before completion.
Security review should focus on authorization and secret handling.
Documentation updates are needed because the feature adds a new environment variable.

best_practices: Run the gates at each stage instead of saving all checks for the end.
Treat security, tests, and build failures as blockers until they are resolved or explicitly approved.
Pair automated validator output with manual review for authorization and business logic.
anti_patterns: Using the checklist as proof of safety without running relevant project commands.
Bypassing failed gates without a written reason, issue link, and user approval.
Applying every example mechanically to projects that use different frameworks.

faq.question: Does this skill run all checks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It includes guidance, command examples, and a validator aggregator that depends on related scripts being installed.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits TypeScript, React, Next.js, Prisma, and Vitest-style projects best.

faq.question: Can it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure security checks, but authorization and data exposure still need manual review.

faq.question: Does it require Bash access?
faq.answer: Some validation steps use shell commands and the included Python script calls local validators.

faq.question: How should Claude or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Use it as a staged checklist before implementation, during coding, after tests, and before final delivery.

faq.question: What should happen when a gate fails?
faq.answer: Fix the issue before continuing, or document an approved exception with a follow-up plan.
